issues.description: Unknown Slurm states are treated as terminal, so nonterminal states like CONFIGURING or REQUEUED can block later RUNNING updates.
Upsert conflict resolution ignores record timestamps, allowing older same-rank terminal snapshots to overwrite newer terminal data.
Rows are considered unchanged using only state, end, and elapsed_sec, so corrected user, partition, CPU, GPU, or exit_code fields are silently ignored.
The default SQLite database and parent directory are created with process umask permissions, which may expose user/job accounting data on shared systems.
Schema has no versioning or migration mechanism, making future changes risky once real databases exist.
No indexes support reference-time, state, partition, or user report queries, so reports will degrade to table scans as the job table grows.
Negative AllocCPUS and GPU counts are accepted, producing impossible negative usage totals.
Empty User and Partition fields are accepted and stored, causing blank report groups instead of rejecting malformed accounting rows.
Rows with no usable submit, start, or end timestamp can be stored but are invisible to normal since-filtered reports.
Ingest only handles missing files and malformed headers; permission, decoding, SQLite, and directory errors can surface as raw tracebacks.
top_users assumes newest_reference_time is parseable ISO text and can crash if malformed or timezone-mixed values reach the database.
Project configuration has no linting, formatting, type-checking, or coverage settings, so quality gates rely only on the existing pytest suite.
